# New in PocketOne

PocketOne does everything PocketBase does, and adds the features below. They're all built into the `pocketone`
binary, and most are on by default. There's nothing to install.

Three of them set PocketOne apart: hooks with `async`, `import` and TypeScript,
async pages in TSX, and hundreds of apps running as isolates in one process.

## Modern JavaScript on the server

**[Hooks with async, import and TypeScript](https://pocketone.dev/docs/quickjs).** Your `pb_hooks` run on QuickJS with the same JS API you
already use, plus:

- `async` handlers and `await`. The app keeps serving other requests while a handler waits on the database or an HTTP
  call.
- ES modules: `import` and `export` between your files, and packages from `node_modules`.
- TypeScript: write `.pb.ts` files and they run as they are.
- Globals shared by every handler, and memory and time limits that stop a runaway script instead of the app.

```ts
// pb_hooks/orders.pb.ts
import { total } from "./lib/pricing.mjs"

routerAdd("GET", "/api/orders/{id}/total", async (e) => {
  const order = await e.app.findRecordById.async("orders", e.request.pathValue("id"))
  return e.json(200, { total: total(order) })
})
```

**[Pages in TSX, TypeScript or EJS](https://pocketone.dev/docs/features/sites).** Put a `.tsx`, `.jsx`, `.ejs` or `.md` file in `pb_pages`
and it's a server-rendered page, with your records a function call away. Components `import` each other, and a page's
code and endpoints are `.ts` files beside them. Every part of a page can `await`: loaders, handlers, middleware, EJS tags and
`async` components, and sibling components render at the same time. esbuild is built into the binary: no Node, no
`npm install`, no build step.

```tsx
// pb_pages/products/[id].tsx
import Price from './_private/Price'

export default async function Product({ ctx }: any) {
  const product = await ctx.app.findRecordById.async('products', ctx.params.id)
  return (
    <article>
      <h1>{product.getString('name')}</h1>
      <Price cents={product.getInt('price')} />
    </article>
  )
}
```

## Hundreds of apps in one process

**[PocketBase isolates](https://pocketone.dev/docs/features/isolates).** One `pocketone` process runs hundreds of PocketBase apps as
isolates, routed by hostname. Each is a complete app with its own data, hooks and dashboard. It starts on its first
request in tens of milliseconds, costs about 3 MB while it runs, and is sandboxed from the others: its own memory cap,
time limits, files, SQL and secrets. No container per app, no idle memory to pay for.

```yaml
# pocketone.yaml: every hostname you ask for becomes its own app (dev mode)
multisite: {}
instances: { dev: true }
pocker: { root: ./pb_root }
```

## Everything new at a glance

| | What you get |
|---|---|
| [QuickJS hooks](https://pocketone.dev/docs/quickjs) | `async`/`await`, ES module `import`, TypeScript, shared globals and hard limits, on the same JS API |
| [Pages](https://pocketone.dev/docs/features/sites) | Server-rendered pages in TSX, JSX, TypeScript, EJS or Markdown, with `await` everywhere and no build step |
| [PocketBase isolates](https://pocketone.dev/docs/features/isolates) | Hundreds of apps in one process, each starting in tens of ms, about 3 MB each, sandboxed |
| [Point-in-time restore](https://pocketone.dev/docs/features/restore) | Every change recorded; restore to any second in the last 72 hours, and undo the restore |
| [Deploy and live sync](https://pocketone.dev/docs/features/deploy) | `pocketone deploy` uploads only what changed; `pocketone dev` syncs a folder both ways and streams logs |
| [Remote CLI](https://pocketone.dev/docs/features/remote) | Admin commands against any app, from your terminal, a script or an agent |
| [API tokens and OAuth](https://pocketone.dev/docs/features/tokens) | Named, scoped tokens you revoke one by one; your app is an OAuth server |
| [MCP for AI agents](https://pocketone.dev/docs/features/mcp) | `/mcp` on every app, with OAuth sign-in and your own tools from `pb_hooks` |
| [Bulk mail](https://pocketone.dev/docs/features/bulk-mail) | Campaigns from the dashboard, with unsubscribes, suppression and pacing |
| [Desktop apps](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/desktop) | The same folder builds into native macOS, Windows and Linux apps with `pocketone desktop build`, each user's data on their machine (preview) |
| [pocketone.yaml](https://pocketone.dev/docs/pocketone-yaml) | One config file, with every extension's options and a `.env` for secrets |

Each page shows the feature in the dashboard, from your terminal and from an agent. For how a feature works or how to
build on it, follow its **How it works** links to the [extension](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/all) pages.

## Also built in

Smaller additions you'll notice without a page of their own:

- **Mail you can see in dev mode:** with `serve --dev` and no SMTP settings, mail is caught and shown at
  `http://127.0.0.1:8025` instead of being sent ([Mail Trap](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/mailtrap)).
- **S3 redirects:** files kept in S3 download straight from the bucket through short-lived signed links
  ([S3 Redirect](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/s3redirect)).
- **Restylable sign-in pages:** copy the OAuth sign-in screens into your app with `pocketone template eject` and edit
  them ([Templates](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/templates)).
- **Settings and cache:** one settings screen and one shared memory budget for every feature
  ([Settings](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/settings), [Cache](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/cache)).

Coming from PocketBase? [What stays the same, and how each feature compares](https://pocketone.dev/docs/pocketbase).
